乃木でもない。Fでもな

world.title: September offers prime planet views for local stargazers
world.description: September is shaping up to be a strong month for local planet watchers, with several planets visible in Saskatchewan’s morning and evening sky. Abigail Sadowski, resident astronomer at Kalium Observatory, said Mars, Jupiter, Venus, Mercury, Saturn and Neptune will all be visible at different times throughout the month. Morning planets Mars will be visible throughout September for those willing to stay up late and get up early. “It rises at around 1:30 in the morning and remains visible until sunrise,” Sadowski said, adding that viewers should look toward the east. Jupiter will also be visible in the early morning. At the beginning of September, it rises around 4 a.m. in the northeast.
